name: EIA weekly natural gas storage report trading

origin.source_title: Natural gas prices and the gas storage report: Public news and volatility in energy futures markets (Journal of Futures Markets)

how_it_works.simple: Every Thursday the US says how much natural gas went into or out of storage. Gas prices swing hard right after, depending on whether the number beat guesses.
how_it_works.analogy: Like a school posting exam results at a set time: everyone reacts in the same few minutes.
how_it_works.precise: The storage surprise is the reported weekly injection or withdrawal minus the analyst consensus. Linn and Zhu find volatility of NYMEX natural gas futures spikes at the release and stays high for about 30 minutes. Gay, Simkins and Turac show the market weights individual analyst forecasts by their past accuracy when forming the expectation.

rule: At the Thursday 10:30 ET EIA storage release, compute surprise = actual net change minus consensus; go short front-month natural gas futures if the build is larger than expected (or the draw smaller), long in the opposite case; exit within 30 minutes. A volatility variant buys short-dated options before the release.
data_needed: EIA Weekly Natural Gas Storage Report history (free)
Intraday NYMEX natural gas futures prices
Weather (heating and cooling degree days) as a control
economic_rationale: Storage is the main public signal of the gas supply and demand balance, so news moves prices (Linn and Zhu 2004; Hu, Hu and Lin 2014).
why_it_might_fail: Most of the move happens within minutes and expectations already embed analyst forecasts (Gay, Simkins and Turac 2009); weather shocks also drive prices and can swamp the storage signal (Hu, Hu and Lin 2014).

reported_results.source: Linn and Zhu (2004), Journal of Futures Markets abstract
reported_results.notes: Volatility study, not a trading backtest: the storage report caused considerable volatility at release and for up to 30 minutes after. No return figures in the abstract. Read via the OpenAlex record.

reported_results.source: Hu, Hu and Lin (2014), The Scientific World Journal (full text via Europe PMC PMC4122141)
reported_results.market: Near and far month natural gas futures, daily
reported_results.notes: Storage announcements significantly affect natural gas futures returns; expected inventory surprises negatively affect far-month returns; volatility is higher on Thursdays. No Sharpe or return figures for a trading rule.

relevance.reason: A scheduled energy news event, but natural gas has little direct link to major currencies, so it is mainly a template for event handling.
